findingsBeforeAnyEdit.title: The slate is not a hauska-factory artifact — it is out of this lane's registered write scope entirely
findingsBeforeAnyEdit.detail: readParcelRecord (hauska-engine services/retrieval-api/src/parcel-record-reader.ts) checks PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE.has(`${countyFips}:${railKey}`) against services/retrieval-api/src/parcel-record-slate.json. That file's own header says it is 'Vendored copy of legacy-design-tools artifacts/api-server/src/lib/parcelRecordAllowlist.ts's PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE ... Re-sync both this file and legacy-design-tools's own copy together.' The CANONICAL slate is therefore in legacy-design-tools, the VENDORED copy in hauska-engine. Neither repo is in this lane's dispatch ('Where you work: hauska-factory-p152-slate ... and hauska-map-p152-slate'). hauska-factory owns only the GATE VERDICT (parcel_gate_verdict, written by publish-gate-sched.mjs) — a real, separate control, per OPS-21 preamble's own 'grading is not serving' section. Running the gate is in scope; writing the slate is not.
findingsBeforeAnyEdit.action: Do not create an ad-hoc hauska-engine or legacy-design-tools worktree. Read-verify the gate (in scope) and hand off the exact slate diff for the owning seat/lane to apply.

findingsBeforeAnyEdit.title: Five of the ten named rails are architecturally NOT independent slate candidates
findingsBeforeAnyEdit.detail: legacy-design-tools' parcelRecordAllowlist.ts documents, at length, that zoningJurisdictionKey and zoningProvenance are siblings of the representative key zoningDistrict, and setbackSideFt/setbackRearFt/setbackCornerFt are siblings of the representative key setbackFrontFt. Its own comment: 'these three have NO resolveAllowlist call site of their own anywhere in this repo ... A slate entry literally spelled "<county>:setbackSideFt" would never be read by any code.' That is true for LDT's consumers. It is NOT true for hauska-engine's retrieval-api reader, which iterates every PARCEL_RECORD_RAIL_KEYS independently with no group/representative-key concept at all — readParcelRecord will happily classify setbackSideFt as record the moment a literal '<county>:setbackSideFt' slate entry exists and its own per-rail gate verdict passes. This is a genuine architecture mismatch between the two consumers sharing one 'verbatim-synced' slate file, not something this lane should resolve unilaterally by appending strings to two files it does not own.
findingsBeforeAnyEdit.action: Report precisely; do not silently patch. Named in the close as a design question for whoever owns both the reader and the allowlist.

findingsBeforeAnyEdit.title: Mission item 2 (panel dollar rails + owner gated in the BFF) is already true in production
findingsBeforeAnyEdit.detail: Live anonymous GET https://smartsite.cloud/api/spine/property-atoms/<id>/facets, all five OPS-23 probe parcels, 2026-09-13T19:39Z: facets.baseFacts.cadRoll.{marketValue,assessedValue,landValue,improvementValue} and ownerFact all return {state:'refused', code:'studio-gated', reason:'...Studio or Team only...'} — never a value, never null, never a blank. Built by P152-PANEL (cadRoll: atom-chain-to-facets.cadroll.test.ts, PR #390). The gate lives at legacy-design-tools cadRollValue.ts/ownerFactRead.ts (single canonical `granted` boolean from subscriptionTierGrantsStudio, forwarded via the PE session cookie the BFF already relays to cortex) — 'the entitlement gate is not yours to change', and there is nothing here that needs changing.
findingsBeforeAnyEdit.action: Do not build a second, redundant gate in the BFF (pe-property-atoms.ts's own module doc: 'a fourth [gate] in the BFF is the defect, not the fix'). Add regression coverage for the one half of this contract with none today (ownerFact; cadRoll already has it) so this correct, already-live behavior cannot silently regress.

findingsBeforeAnyEdit.title: Item 3 (retire by decline) is already generically built for 9 of the 10 rails
findingsBeforeAnyEdit.detail: composeRecordPatch (agValuation, maxImperviousCoverPct, acreageAcres, acreageSqft, acreageMethod) and composeZoningSetbackOverride (zoningJurisdictionKey, zoningProvenance, setbackSideFt, setbackRearFt, setbackCornerFt) already gate strictly on rail.serve === 'record', already leave the legacy/atom-chain value untouched otherwise (verified by reading both functions in full, origin/main). This mechanism activates automatically the moment F-A's slate gap closes. No new hauska-map runtime code is needed for retirement of 9 of the 10 rails. zoningProvenance is the exception: it is tracked in COMPOSED_ZONING_SETBACK_RAIL_KEYS/railStates but its value is applied to no field on ZoningSetbackOverride — no wire field exists to carry it. Slating it would flip its serve state with zero visible effect.
findingsBeforeAnyEdit.action: Do not invent a new wire field for zoningProvenance (out of mandate — 'new values for the rails' is explicitly out of scope, and a new field is closer to new product surface than a value). Add unit coverage proving the other nine, and name the zoningProvenance gap precisely, both in code comments and in the close.

openQuestionsForPlanner: Should a follow-on lane be registered with write access to BOTH legacy-design-tools (parcelRecordAllowlist.ts) and hauska-engine (parcel-record-slate.json) to land the acreageAcres/acreageMethod slate additions this lane verified are safe?
